name: Validation and Repair Loops
question: What happens when the output is wrong?
summary: Validate every structured output against types and business rules, such as a GSTIN format, totals that match their line items, or dates in range. When validation fails, send the specific error back to the model and ask for a corrected output, at most once or twice, then fall back: a human queue, a partial result or a clear failure. Generic “try again” retries waste calls; specific errors fix most problems in one round.
useCases: Outputs written to ledgers, CRMs or other systems of record
Extraction where some rules cannot be expressed in the schema
Pipelines that must never drop a record silently

steps.title: First attempt, strictly structured
steps.text: The model returns an object that matches the schema’s shape, as in the previous technique.

steps.title: Validate the business rules
steps.text: Invoice adds validators: the GSTIN format and totals that match their items. 17% of first attempts fail one of them.

steps.title: Send the exact error back
steps.text: The model sees its own answer and the specific message, such as “total 11,800 does not match items summing to 11,200”. Most are fixed in one round.

steps.title: Cap the repairs
steps.text: At most two repairs. Hard inputs would otherwise loop and multiply the cost.

steps.title: Hand over, never drop
steps.text: If it still fails, the invoice goes to a human queue with the reason. Nothing invalid reaches the ledger, and nothing disappears.

steps.title: Log failure types
steps.text: Counting which rules fail most shows what to fix upstream: a clearer description, a schema change or a prompt rule.

library.name: Instructor
library.what: Wraps model clients so outputs are parsed into Pydantic models, and on validation failure re-asks the model with the error, up to max_retries.

practice.note: Catch the final validation exception and route the record to a human queue; never write a failed record to the ledger.

numericDrill.question: 17.2% of first outputs fail validation. Each repair with the specific error succeeds 70% of the time. With up to two repairs, what share of records still fails, in percent?
numericDrill.answer: 17.2% × 0.3 × 0.3 = 1.55%. One repair leaves 5.2%, two leave 1.55%, and a third would leave about 0.46%. Those go to a human queue rather than the ledger.

interview.question: Why send the validation error back rather than just retrying?
interview.answer: A plain retry repeats the same conditions, so the model often makes the same mistake. The specific error, such as “total 11,800 does not match items summing to 11,200”, tells it exactly what to fix, and most outputs are corrected in one round.

interview.question: What should happen when repairs run out?
interview.answer: Stop and hand over: put the record in a human queue with the error, or return a partial result marked as incomplete. Never write an invalid record to a system of record, and never drop it silently. Track failure types to fix the prompt or schema at the source.
